derivations.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths $s_j$ of the axes $j$ before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

Define $\Phi:\mathbb C[x]/(x^S-1)\to\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_i^{s_i}-1)$ by $x\mapsto\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i}$, with one variable $x_i$ per axis. Since $s_i\mid S$, each $x_i^{\mu_iS}=1$, so $\Phi$ respects $x^S=1$ and defines an algebra map.

Then $\Phi(x^k)=1$ exactly when $s_i\mid\mu_ik$ for every $i$; as $\mu_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$ this means $s_i\mid k$ for every $i$, and as the $s_i$ are pairwise coprime, $S\mid k$. So the image of $x$ has order $S$ and its $S$ powers are distinct. The target has exactly $S$ monomials, so the powers run through all of them exactly once. Hence $\Phi$ is an isomorphism and preserves [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md).

Write $k=\sum_ja_jP_j$ in mixed radix, with digits $0\le a_j<s_j$. The axis-$i$ coordinate $b_i$ of $\Phi(x^k)$ is $\mu_ik\bmod s_i$. Terms with $j>i$ vanish modulo $s_i$, since $s_i$ divides $P_j$, and $\mu_iP_i\equiv1$ modulo $s_i$. Hence $b_i=a_i+\mu_i\sum_{j<i}a_jP_j\pmod{s_i}$, which depends only on lower-index digits.
Terms with $j>i$ vanish modulo $s_i$, since $s_i$ divides $P_j$, and $\mu_iP_i\equiv1$ modulo $s_i$. Hence $b_i=a_i+\mu_i\sum_{j<i}a_jP_j\pmod{s_i}$, which depends only on lower-index digits.

Update the targets for $i=d,d-1,\dots,1$, so no lower-index control has yet changed when axis $i$ is updated and the offset is computed from the original digits. Each update is a prefix-controlled cyclic shift of the valid interval $[0,s_i)$ and the identity on $[s_i,t_i)$, so zero padding stays zero.

Axes have $\ell$ or $\ell-1$ address bits; for unequal widths, move the longer axis's leading bit aside, swap the equal-width remainder, and restore the bit, adding a fixed number of linear passes. Reversing $d$ axes takes $O(d^2)$ such moves, so reordering dominates the $O(dTp)$ shifts and $O(Tp)$ scans. The inverse subtracts the same offsets for $i=1,\dots,d$, then reorders back and deletes the padding. The map, its inverse and the padding cost $O(Tp\,d^2(1+\ell^\tau))$

The map is implemented by these shifts, each of linear cost by [Controlled shifts and rational scalings](controlled-shifts.md).

symbols.name: axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of prime cyclic axes, with no coefficient axis counted.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the number of prime cyclic axes (unlike on the cyclic-convolution page, no coefficient axis is counted), $i$ index them, and $s_1,\dots,s_d$ be pairwise coprime axis lengths (these $s_i$ are unrelated to the chirp page's multipliers).

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The length of prime cyclic axis i; the s_i are pairwise coprime.

symbols.name: prefix product

symbols.name: coordinate exponent
symbols.meaning: The inverse of P_i modulo s_i, the exponent of x_i in the image of x.

symbols.name: address map
symbols.meaning: The ring isomorphism sending x to the product of x_i^{mu_i}.

symbols.name: axis variable
symbols.meaning: The variable of axis i in the multi-axis ring.

symbols.name: coefficient index
symbols.meaning: A single coefficient index, an exponent of x; not an output index tuple as on the multidimensional-transform page.
symbols.quote: The letter $k$ changes meaning here: it is a single coefficient index, an exponent of $x$, not an output index tuple as on the multidimensional-transform page.

symbols.name: mixed-radix digit
symbols.meaning: The digit of k of weight P_j, with 0<=a_j<s_j.
symbols.quote: Write $k=\sum_ja_jP_j$ in mixed radix, with digits $0\le a_j<s_j$.

symbols.name: digit index
symbols.meaning: The index of an axis before axis i, in the product defining P_i, and later the index of a mixed-radix digit.
symbols.quote: Let $P_i=\prod_{j<i}s_j$ be the product of the lengths $s_j$ of the axes $j$ before axis $i$, and $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}\pmod{s_i}$.

symbols.name: axis coordinate
symbols.quote: The axis-$i$ coordinate $b_i$ of $\Phi(x^k)$ is $\mu_ik\bmod s_i$.

symbols.name: address bits
symbols.meaning: The number of address bits of an axis of length r.
symbols.quote: Pad axis $i$ with zero records to a length $t_i$, a power of two with $r/2\le t_i\le r$, where $r=2^\ell$ is the record length, so $\ell$ is the number of address bits of an axis of length $r$.

symbols.name: padded record count
symbols.meaning: The number of padded records, the product of the padded axis lengths t_i.
symbols.quote: Let $T=\prod_it_i$ be the number of padded records, each of $O(p)$ bits.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 in the chunk-interchange cost.
symbols.quote: Let $V=Tp$ be the stream volume and $\tau<1$ a fixed exponent.

symbols.name: axis index
symbols.meaning: The index of a prime cyclic axis, from 1 to d.

symbols.name: padded axis length
symbols.meaning: The length of axis i after zero padding, a power of two between r/2 and r.
